content.text: The setting of an app/image refers to the universe/storyline in which the action takes place.

content.heading: Pixelated or Childlike Style
content.text: A childlike style is more likely to appeal to younger children. Such a style may include (but is not limited to): A fantastical theme Bright colors Playful music Cheerful sounds and/or An overall cartoon-like atmosphere A pixelated style is one in which characters appear blocky, such as in an early arcade or retro game. This refers to how reactions to violent acts are portrayed.
A violent act might be interpreted differently based on how close a user is to the action and how frequently this content occurs.
This section describes how much blood and/or gore is associated with the acts of violence.

content.heading: Realistic or Historical War Setting
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" if the app/image has a realistic war setting as its main theme. This includes historic and recent as well as ongoing military or political conflicts. This question must also be confirmed for products with fictional conflicts or in which some historical facts are altered as long as the setting or storyline is rooted in real life events. Submitters should answer "No" if the app/image only references war in text or dialogue or where only a small portion of the gameplay takes place within a war scenario. War themes set in the distant future or in purely fictional universes without any parallels to history or present should also not be indicated here.

content.heading: Violence Towards Vulnerable or Defenseless Characters
content.text: Innocent characters are defined as bystanders that are not necessarily involved in the app's objective. The uninvolved characters must be visibly vulnerable to the attacks by either being permanently injured or killed. If the app/image actively encourages the killing of defenseless characters, this aspect must always be confirmed with "Yes." This also includes any mass killings of innocent characters, such as where groups of characters are killed or injured at random for no apparent reason and deals with themes such as the killing of pedestrians on the street, shoppers in a shopping arcade, or children in a school. These actions occur "without consequences" when the perpetrator is able to commit them without penalty or drawback. These actions occur "with consequences" when something negative occurs to the perpetrator (e.g., the app/image restarts after shooting a civilian, police arrest a character after the character drives through and kills a crowd of bystanders). Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Fierce Sounds, Dark Overtones, or Disturbing Elements
content.text: The violence in the app/image is accompanied by loud explosions, screams and/or fearsome characters. Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Referred To
content.text: Some apps might not have violence as part the focus of the app, but instead have a storyline or plot point involving a violent act that is communicated strictly as described - not visually, but referred to via text or dialogue such as a newspaper headline referring to a murder or two characters discussing a foiled assassination plot. Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Implied
content.text: This is where users do not actually see the violence against humans, but it is obvious that it is happening. It covers such matters as the bombing of a city where users know civilians are killed or injured, blowing up a tank or shooting down a plane where users know that the crew is killed, smashing into cars or other vehicles where the driver/passenger must be injured. content.text: The violence is seen, but from a distant perspective. Characters shown take up a small portion of the screen. Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Interactive Use of Illegal Drugs
content.text: The user's input may influence actions and/or the character can actively choose to use drugs and/or control the drug use. For example, the user can choose whether or not to light a joint or bong or control the amount of the drug to consume. A character simply touching, running into or past a depiction of a drug in an app/image would typically not satisfy this criteria.

content.heading: Encourages/Glamorizes
content.text: If characters gain advantage or achieve success after the use of illegal/recreational drugs, this would be considered encouragement/glamorization.

guideline.title: Fantasy Drugs
guideline.rawText: Fantasy drugs are drugs that do not exist in real life but mirror the effects of real-word drugs. A fantasy drug affects characters in ways that appear similar to how real-world drugs might behave. References to modern drug terminology/slang (e.g., "getting high," "junkie," "dealer") or depictions of drug paraphernalia/accessories (e.g., vials, syringes, bongs) are usually indicators that the fantasy drugs mirror real-word drugs. Items such as healing/health potions and mushroom power-ups would not be considered fantasy drugs without these references or depictions.

content.heading: Realistic or Historical War Setting
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" if the app/image has a realistic war setting as its main theme. This includes historic and recent as well as ongoing military or political conflicts. This question must also be confirmed for products with fictional conflicts or in which some historical facts are altered as long as the setting or storyline is rooted in real life events. Submitters should answer "No" if the app/image only references war in text or dialogue or where only a small portion of the gameplay takes place within a war scenario. War themes set in the distant future or in purely fictional universes without any parallels to history or present should also not be indicated here.

content.heading: Violence Towards Vulnerable or Defenseless Characters
content.text: Innocent characters are defined as bystanders that are not necessarily involved in the app's objective. If a realistically depicted character reacts to violence in an exaggerated or nonsensical way, this would still be considered an unrealistic portrayal of violence despite the fact that the character may appear "photorealistic" in depiction.

content.heading: User Content
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" to this question if users can freely exchange content they have created. This includes the ability to communicate between users, comment on provided content, share photos, or exchange any other type of content created by users. In this section, submitters should describe policies related to user interaction and user-created content shared within the app. To help define an online interaction or content exchange, developers should only consider their app's native services and not consider sharing that is accomplished by using secondary apps (such as Facebook or twitter). content.heading: Online Content
content.text: Use this section to discuss content that is featured or promoted in the app, but isn’t part of the initial download and isn’t generated by users. Examples of this type of content are movies in the Netflix app, product listings in the Amazon Shopping app, songs in the Spotify app, or news articles in the New York Times app. If content can be downloaded and cached for later use, that should still be disclosed in this section. Questions in this section are policy-based to reflect the fact that this content is dynamic in nature. For example, Hulu may not know the content of their future catalog, but it can predict that it won’t feature pornography. Similarly, the Guardian may not know what stories it will write in the future, but it does have editorial policies in place and can use those policies to determine how to fill out these questions. Please note that content users import into the app/image themselves would not be considered featured or promoted. For example, if you are submitting a music player you do not have to consider the .mp3s that a user may already have downloaded on their device. content.heading: Realistic or Historical War Setting
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" if the app/image has a realistic war setting as its main theme. This includes historic and recent as well as ongoing military or political conflicts. This question must also be confirmed for products with fictional conflicts or in which some historical facts are altered as long as the setting or storyline is rooted in real life events. Submitters should answer "No" if the app/image only references war in text or dialogue or where only a small portion of the gameplay takes place within a war scenario. War themes set in the distant future or in purely fictional universes without any parallels to history or present should also not be indicated here.

content.heading: Violence Towards Vulnerable or Defenseless Characters
content.text: Innocent characters are defined as bystanders that are not necessarily involved in the app's objective. The uninvolved characters must be visibly vulnerable to the attacks by either being permanently injured or killed. If the app/image actively encourages the killing of defenseless characters, this aspect must always be confirmed with "Yes." This also includes any mass killings of innocent characters, such as where groups of characters are killed or injured at random for no apparent reason and deals with themes such as the killing of pedestrians on the street, shoppers in a shopping arcade, or children in a school. These actions occur "without consequences" when the perpetrator is able to commit them without penalty or drawback. These actions occur "with consequences" when something negative occurs to the perpetrator (e.g., the app/image restarts after shooting a civilian, police arrest a character after the character drives through and kills a crowd of bystanders). Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Mild/Limited

content.heading: Moderate
content.text: There is more blood than just the minimum required to communicate an event (such as that seen at the Mild/Limited level) or some mild dismemberment, but some restraint in the volume, frequency, and realism is still shown. Examples include the following: Brief puffs of blood that indicate that the target was hit, and also bloodstains appear on the surface of the character and on the surface of the wall behind the target Explosions that cause characters to burst into small chunks that are somewhat distant from the viewer Frequent depictions of large bloodstains on the floor An app/image that allows users to continue triggering blood effects on dead bodies A depiction of an impalement with limited blood Example 1Example 2

content.heading: High
content.text: Blood and/or gore are major components of the app. Whether by sheer volume, realism of the depiction, or intensity, the level of blood and/or gore in these apps stands out. content.heading: Realistic or Historical War Setting
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" if the app/image has a realistic war setting as its main theme. This includes historic and recent as well as ongoing military or political conflicts. This question must also be confirmed for products with fictional conflicts or in which some historical facts are altered as long as the setting or storyline is rooted in real life events. Submitters should answer "No" if the app/image only references war in text or dialogue or where only a small portion of the gameplay takes place within a war scenario. War themes set in the distant future or in purely fictional universes without any parallels to history or present should also not be indicated here.

content.heading: Violence Towards Vulnerable or Defenseless Characters
content.text: Innocent characters are defined as bystanders that are not necessarily involved in the app's objective. The uninvolved characters must be visibly vulnerable to the attacks by either being permanently injured or killed. If the app/image actively encourages the killing of defenseless characters, this aspect must always be confirmed with "Yes." This also includes any mass killings of innocent characters, such as where groups of characters are killed or injured at random for no apparent reason and deals with themes such as the killing of pedestrians on the street, shoppers in a shopping arcade, or children in a school. These actions occur "without consequences" when the perpetrator is able to commit them without penalty or drawback. These actions occur "with consequences" when something negative occurs to the perpetrator (e.g., the app/image restarts after shooting a civilian, police arrest a character after the character drives through and kills a crowd of bystanders). Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Mild/Limited
content.text: While there is some blood, its use is constrained to very limited and purposeful uses. Examples include the following: Infrequent pools of static blood indicating that a murder took place at that location Brief puffs of blood that indicate that the target has been hit. Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Moderate
content.text: There is more blood than just the minimum required to communicate an event (such as that seen at the Mild/Limited level) or some mild dismemberment, but some restraint in the volume, frequency, and realism is still shown. Examples include the following: Brief puffs of blood that indicate that the target was hit, and also bloodstains appear on the surface of the character and on the surface of the wall behind the target Explosions that cause characters to burst into small chunks that are somewhat distant from the viewer Frequent depictions of large bloodstains on the floor An app/image that allows users to continue triggering blood effects on dead bodies A depiction of an impalement with limited blood Example 1Example 2

content.heading: High
content.text: Blood and/or gore are major components of the app. Whether by sheer volume, realism of the depiction, or intensity, the level of blood and/or gore in these apps stands out. Examples include: A depiction of large sprays of blood after someone is slashed with a sword A scene depicting the dismemberment of a character with graphic detail Example 1Example 2

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.text: These are post-action visuals such as coming upon a dead body. While no violent act is shown, the images suggest that a violent act has taken place.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Limited Detail
content.text: Limited injuries may be shown, such as minimal cuts and bruising.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Moderate Detail
content.text: Injuries may be shown, such as puncture wounds and missing limbs. There should be no strong and realistic gory images, such as a close focus on graphic wounds or graphic sight of mutilated or dismembered bodies.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Graphic Detail
content.text: This includes the most graphic and realistic sight of injuries and gore, in the aftermath of a violent act, such as a close focus on realistic gaping wounds, sight of exposed internal organs hanging out, and bodies that have been dismembered or mutilated (e.g., skin having been peeled off).

content.heading: Realistic or Historical War Setting
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" if the app/image has a realistic war setting as its main theme. This includes historic and recent as well as ongoing military or political conflicts. This question must also be confirmed for products with fictional conflicts or in which some historical facts are altered as long as the setting or storyline is rooted in real life events. Submitters should answer "No" if the app/image only references war in text or dialogue or where only a small portion of the gameplay takes place within a war scenario. War themes set in the distant future or in purely fictional universes without any parallels to history or present should also not be indicated here.

content.heading: Violence Towards Vulnerable or Defenseless Characters
content.text: Innocent characters are defined as bystanders that are not necessarily involved in the app's objective. The uninvolved characters must be visibly vulnerable to the attacks by either being permanently injured or killed. If the app/image actively encourages the killing of defenseless characters, this aspect must always be confirmed with "Yes." This also includes any mass killings of innocent characters, such as where groups of characters are killed or injured at random for no apparent reason and deals with themes such as the killing of pedestrians on the street, shoppers in a shopping arcade, or children in a school. These actions occur "without consequences" when the perpetrator is able to commit them without penalty or drawback. These actions occur "with consequences" when something negative occurs to the perpetrator (e.g., the app/image restarts after shooting a civilian, police arrest a character after the character drives through and kills a crowd of bystanders). content.heading: Mild/Limited
content.text: While there is some blood, its use is constrained to very limited and purposeful uses. Examples include the following: Infrequent pools of static blood indicating that a murder took place at that location Brief puffs of blood that indicate that the target has been hit. Example 1Example 2

content.heading: Moderate
content.text: There is more blood than just the minimum required to communicate an event (such as that seen at the Mild/Limited level) or some mild dismemberment, but some restraint in the volume, frequency, and realism is still shown. Examples include the following: Brief puffs of blood that indicate that the target was hit, and also bloodstains appear on the surface of the character and on the surface of the wall behind the target Explosions that cause characters to burst into small chunks that are somewhat distant from the viewer Frequent depictions of large bloodstains on the floor An app/image that allows users to continue triggering blood effects on dead bodies A depiction of an impalement with limited blood Example 1Example 2

content.heading: High
content.text: Blood and/or gore are major components of the app. Whether by sheer volume, realism of the depiction, or intensity, the level of blood and/or gore in these apps stands out. Examples include: A depiction of large sprays of blood after someone is slashed with a sword A scene depicting the dismemberment of a character with graphic detail Example 1Example 2

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.text: These are post-action visuals such as coming upon a dead body. While no violent act is shown, the images suggest that a violent act has taken place.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Limited Detail
content.text: Limited injuries may be shown, such as minimal cuts and bruising.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Moderate Detail
content.text: Injuries may be shown, such as puncture wounds and missing limbs. There should be no strong and realistic gory images, such as a close focus on graphic wounds or graphic sight of mutilated or dismembered bodies.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Graphic Detail
content.text: This includes the most graphic and realistic sight of injuries and gore, in the aftermath of a violent act, such as a close focus on realistic gaping wounds, sight of exposed internal organs hanging out, and bodies that have been dismembered or mutilated (e.g., skin having been peeled off).

options.text: Blood that isn't directly related to a violent act (e.g., blood on clothing, blood in the background, blood resulting from performing surgery)

content.heading: Blood Unrelated to Violent Acts
content.text: These are situations where there is blood, but the blood is not directly connected to a violent action. For example, there may be blood on a character's shirt or there may be blood that is occurring as a result of performing surgery.

content.heading: Obscured/Innuendo
content.text: Submitters should select "obscured" if the sex act is either entirely off-camera or completely blocked from view. In these situations, the user understands that some kind of sex act is happening but cannot see it. Example 1Example 2

options.text: Shown with No Nudity - Characters are depicted in a sexual act but no nudity is shown

content.heading: Shown with No Nudity
content.text: Submitters should select "shown with no nudity" if characters are depicted in a sexual act but without any nudity shown. In these situations the user can visually identify that a specific sexual act is taking place, but no nudity or partial nudity is depicted. Example 1Example 2

options.text: Shown with Partial Nudity - Breasts, Buttocks

content.heading: Shown with Partial Nudity
content.text: Submitters should select "shown with partial nudity" if characters are depicted in a sexual act featuring partial nudity. Naked breasts and buttocks would be considered partial nudity even if they are only on screen for a short time and even if they are not fully exposed.

content.heading: Shown with Full Frontal Nudity
content.text: Submitters should select "shown with full frontal nudity" if characters are depicted in a sexual act featuring full frontal nudity. Penises, vaginas, and displays of pubic hair would be considered full frontal nudity even if they are only on screen for a short time.

options.text: Suggestive references and innuendo in text, dialogue, or heard

guideline.title: Suggestive References or Innuendo
guideline.rawText: These are suggestive or provocative references that can be indirect. Romantic dialogue such as "I'm in love," "I'm going to try to go out with him," or "She's the prettiest girl I've ever seen" would NOT be considered suggestive.

content.text: These are suggestive or provocative references that can be indirect. Romantic dialogue such as "I'm in love," "I'm going to try to go out with him," or "She's the prettiest girl I've ever seen" would NOT be considered suggestive.

options.text: Overtly sexual situations or visually depicted innuendo

guideline.title: Overtly Sexual Situations
guideline.rawText: These are situations that are sexual but do not culminate in the depiction of a sex act. Examples include lap dances, bedroom scenes that depict the before and after of an implied sex act, photos of scantily clad characters that are depicted in sexually suggestive poses, or any scenes that create sexual tension without necessarily having explicitly sexual dialogue.

content.heading: Online Content
content.text: Use this section to discuss content that is featured or promoted in the app, but isn’t part of the initial download and isn’t generated by users. Examples of this type of content are movies in the Netflix app, product listings in the Amazon Shopping app, songs in the Spotify app, or news articles in the New York Times app. If content can be downloaded and cached for later use, that should still be disclosed in this section. Questions in this section are policy-based to reflect the fact that this content is dynamic in nature. For example, Hulu may not know the content of their future catalog, but it can predict that it won’t feature pornography. Similarly, the Guardian may not know what stories it will write in the future, but it does have editorial policies in place and can use those policies to determine how to fill out these questions. content.heading: Displays User's Location to Others
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" only if the app/image transmits the user's current, precise location to other people. Broad location information (e.g, "New York City," "Germany," "Leicester Square") is not specific enough to be considered precise. Essentially, if users of the app/image could find each other in the real world based on information provided by the app, then this question should be marked "Yes." This includes apps that share users' locations within the app/image itself (e.g., an app/image that displays the location of all users of the app/image on a map) or broadcast users' location data to other apps (e.g., an app/image posting your location to a social network). Submitters should not say "Yes" if the app/image merely uses the users' location but does not share it with others. Examples of functions that would not trigger a "Yes" to this question would be accessing a user's location to provide driving instruction, using a user's location to recommend nearby restaurants or other places of interest, or using a user's location to select a default language of the app.

content.heading: Digital Purchases
content.text: Digital purchases are purchases for digital goods completed directly from within the app. Typically, these purchases are for additional content or premiums. Examples include a game that allows users to unlock additional levels or power-ups for a fee, an app/image that adds additional new features or disables ads when upgraded to a premium edition, or a music player that allows users to purchase downloadable songs.

content.heading: Web Browser/Search Engine
content.text: This question is used to identify web browsers or internet search engines. If your app's primary purpose is as a web browser or search engine and it opens links to content in a webview format or within the app/image instead of an external web browser, you should also answer "Yes." Note that this question should NOT be answered "yes" if your app/image simply contains a link that will open an external web browser.

content.heading: News or Educational
content.text: The primary purpose of the app/image is to present factual information in a neutral way, alert users to current events, or educate users. Apps that mainly focus on sexual advice or instruction (such as "iKamasutra - Sex Positions" or "Best Sex Tips") should not select “Yes” here. The tone and intent of the app/image are important considerations. Content should be presented clinically and in a neutral way. Should the goal of the app/image be to entertain, the product should not be considered “News or Educational.” Examples of apps that should be in this category include Wikipedia, dictionaries, language teaching apps, and medical references such as WebMD and Medscape. Examples of apps that should NOT be categorized as News or Educational include Maxim, The Onion, Urban Dictionary, and Best Sex Tips.

content.heading: Displays User's Location to Others
content.text: Submitters should answer "Yes" only if the app/image transmits the user's current, precise location to other people. Broad location information (e.g, "New York City," "Germany," "Leicester Square") is not specific enough to be considered precise. Essentially, if users of the app/image could find each other in the real world based on information provided by the app, then this question should be marked "Yes." This includes apps that share users' locations within the app/image itself (e.g., an app/image that displays the location of all users of the app/image on a map) or broadcast users' location data to other apps (e.g., an app/image posting your location to a social network). Submitters should not say "Yes" if the app/image merely uses the users' location but does not share it with others. Examples of functions that would not trigger a "Yes" to this question would be accessing a user's location to provide driving instruction, using a user's location to recommend nearby restaurants or other places of interest, or using a user's location to select a default language of the app.

Examples include a game that allows users to unlock additional levels or power-ups for a fee, an app/image that adds additional new features or disables ads when upgraded to a premium edition, or a music player that allows users to purchase downloadable songs.

sequence.section: Disturbing or gory images without a violent act shown.
sequence.text: How explicitly depicted are these disturbing or gory images?

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.text: These are post-action visuals such as coming upon a dead body. While no violent act is shown, the images suggest that a violent act has taken place.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Limited Detail
content.text: Limited injuries may be shown, such as minimal cuts and bruising.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Moderate Detail
content.text: Injuries may be shown, such as puncture wounds and missing limbs. There should be no strong and realistic gory images, such as a close focus on graphic wounds or graphic sight of mutilated or dismembered bodies.

guideline.title: Disturbing or Gory Images without a Violent Act Shown

content.heading: Graphic Detail
content.text: This includes the most graphic and realistic sight of injuries and gore, in the aftermath of a violent act, such as a close focus on realistic gaping wounds, sight of exposed internal organs hanging out, and bodies that have been dismembered or mutilated (e.g., skin having been peeled off).
